subject: New version of Shiny coming soon

messages.author: 55771919c42cb6a1
messages.subject: New version of Shiny coming soon
parts:
Hi everyone -

We're going to release the next version of Shiny, 0.14, in the near future. There are many new features and bug fixes, and we'd appreciate it if you could try it out let us know if you run into any issues. 

To install it, run:

if (!require("devtools"))
  install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("rstudio/shiny")

For more information about the changes, see the NEWS file: https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/master/NEWS.md
(The version there is currently 0.13.2.9005, but we'll increment that to 0.14 when we make the release.)

Thanks!
-Winston

messages.author: 2e8650b38e8cb917
messages.subject: Re: New version of Shiny coming soon
parts:
Hi Winston,
I've been trying to use the newly implemented save function which works great!
However, when an observeEvent is triggered by pressing an actionButton, it is also triggered by the session restore.

library(shiny)

ui = function(request) {
  fluidPage(
    uiOutput("showTest"),
    bookmarkButton()
  )
}
server <- shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  output$showTest <- renderUI({
    actionButton("test", "hi")  
  })
 
  observeEvent(input$test,{
    print('hello')
  })
})

enableBookmarking(store = "url")
shinyApp(ui, server)

The reason is that the value (number of click) is recorded and then restored.You certainly have a reason for programming it like that, but maybe you should give the user the possibility not to save the value of actionButton input? (I guess that many people use actionButtons to trigger an event and are not interested by the input value).
Best regards.

Hi Kevin - 
You can exclude the button from bookmarking by putting setBookmarkExclude("test") in the server function.

Best,
-Winston
